primitives.name: Shot Attribute Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: The attributes are designed to capture the highlevel body movements of a player during the different phases of his shot, e.g., the jump and release.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes SportVU trajectory data provides shot timestamp and spatial coordinates; broadcast video provides ground truth for body pose attributes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when SportVU occlusion exceeds 40% or broadcast video resolution drops below 720p, leading to missing or noisy attribute labels.

layer2.mapping: ShotAttributeAnalysis maps to GSI's Bayesian Hierarchical Model for shot outcome prediction, where latent variables represent hidden body mechanics. It mirrors GSE's state-transition logic by encoding player actions (walk/run/hop) as discrete states in a Markov Decision Process.
layer2.telemetry: Verification metric: Cross-validation accuracy of shot outcome classification using only body pose attributes versus baseline models using only SportVU kinematics.

primitives.name: Chi-Squared Test
primitives.verbatim_quote: Normalized for game context, we use Pearson's Chi-squaredtest toquantify differencesin attributedistributions for made and missed shots, where we observe statistically signi󰅭icant differences in distributions of attributes describing the style of movement, e.g., walk, run, or hop, in various phases of the shot.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$\\chi^2$': 'Dimensionless test statistic', '$O_i$': 'Observed frequency count in bin i', '$E_i$': 'Expected frequency under null hypothesis'}
primitives.assumptions: Data follows multinomial distribution; expected frequencies $E_i > 5$; independence of observations; no structural breaks in shot-taking behavior over time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when sample size is small ($n < 30$) or when multiple comparisons inflate false discovery rate, leading to spurious significance.

layer2.mapping: ChiSquaredTest maps to GSI's Conformal Inference framework for constructing non-parametric prediction intervals on shot success probabilities. It mirrors GSE's hypothesis testing for detecting anomalous player behavior by comparing empirical action distributions against historical baselines.
layer2.telemetry: Verification metric: False positive rate of identifying 'unusual' shot attributes when applied to independent test sets with identical distribution.

primitives.name: Pass Quality
primitives.verbatim_quote: Similarly, with 󰅭ixed shot outcomes, across game contexts, we observe statistically signi󰅭icant differences in distributions of attributes describing the pass quality, direction of movement, and footwork.
primitives.assumptions: Pass quality is measurable through receiver's body posture and timing relative to shot release; game context variables (e.g., score differential, clock) are accurately captured.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when pass trajectory is occluded by defenders, making it impossible to assess receiver's balance and footwork at the moment of catch.

layer2.mapping: PassQuality serves as a feature input to GSI's hierarchical predictive models, informing conditional shot difficulty given pre-shot handling. In GSE, it influences transition probabilities between states (e.g., 'receiving pass' to 'shooting') in reactive planning algorithms.
layer2.telemetry: Verification metric: Correlation between automatically scored pass quality and expert human annotation on a subset of 200 plays.

primitives.name: Stephen Curry Case Study
primitives.verbatim_quote: We also present a case study for Stephen Curry, where we observe that Curry moves much more than the average player in all phases of his shot and he takes a higher proportion of off-balance shots compared to the average player.
primitives.assumptions: Curry's movement patterns are representative of elite shooters; the dataset is balanced across game contexts to avoid confounding variables.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Limitations arise when Curry faces defensive schemes specifically designed to disrupt his typical movement, causing deviations from established behavioral norms.

layer2.mapping: StephenCurryCaseStudy informs GSI's player-specific performance benchmarks and GSE's opponent-aware tactical reasoning, where Curry's unique movement profile is encoded as a distinct behavioral signature.
layer2.telemetry: Verification metric: Out-of-sample prediction accuracy of shot success for Curry versus a control group of similarly skilled players.
